Anna (Support): Hi team — Merridian just reported a bounced ACH with our gateway error: "invalid_routing_number". They insist the ABA is correct. Can we triage?
Merridian Finance: Hey, we sent payout ID pay_98324. Bank responded: "Return: ACH - R01 - Invalid routing number". The routing we provided was "+1 011000015" copied from client system.
Anna (Support): Thanks. Can you paste the exact payload you sent (sanitized)?
Merridian Finance: Sure — payload snippet:
```json
{
  "amount": "12000",
  "currency": "USD",
  "bank_account": {
    "routing_number": "+1\u00A0011000015",
    "account_number": "XXXX1234",
    "account_type": "checking"
  }
}
```
Raj (Payments Eng): Noted the routing_number has "+1" plus a NBSP (\u00A0) between country code and digits. Our normalizer expects digits only and strips whitespace, but NBSP can slip through earlier validations. Also the leading plus may trigger an early-return in the parser.
Lisa (Ops): I see a log entry for payout pay_98324: 
```
2026-11-04T14:03:21Z INFO outgoing_ach payload=... routing_number="+1\u00A0011000015" normalized="+1011000015" status=sent
2026-11-04T14:05:03Z WARN bank_response code=R01 message="Invalid routing number" bank_routing_received="011000015"
```
Raj (Payments Eng): The normalized value in our ledger still had the plus. Downstream router matched by exact string and failed lookup. Should be storing digits-only: `011000015`.
Raj (Payments Eng): Quick repro locally:
```
>>> s = '\\u002b1\u00A0011000015'  # visual plus + NBSP
>>> re.sub(r"[^0-9]", "", s)
'1011000015'
```
Raj (Payments Eng): That produces a leading 1 that becomes part of the routing, turning 011000015 -> 1011000015 (invalid). The correct transformation for international-prefixed strings should drop a leading country code when present (e.g., remove leading '1' if original string had '+1 '), or better: require only 9-digit ABA routing.
Anna (Support): For immediate help: can Merridian resend without the leading +1 and without NBSP? Merridian Finance: We can. Is there a workaround for already-submitted payout?
Lisa (Ops): We can retry the ACH by normalizing on our side then re-sending as a manual remediation, but compliance/consent flag needs approval. I'll open an ops remediation ticket.
Raj (Payments Eng): I'll push a short-term fix to the normalization function in payments-service to always collapse all non-digits then, if length != 9, attempt to strip a leading '1' and re-check length==9 before routing lookup. Proposed code change (hotfix):
```python
def normalize_routing(s):
    # collapse all non-digit chars
    digits = re.sub(r"\D+", "", s)
    if len(digits) == 9:
        return digits
    # if there's a leading country code 1 (e.g. +1 prefix), drop it
    if len(digits) == 10 and digits.startswith('1'):
        return digits[1:]
    raise ValueError('routing_not_9_digits')
```
Raj (Payments Eng): I'll open PR and tag @Lisa for ops rollout.
Anna (Support): Merridian, pls resend the payout after removing the leading +1/any spaces — you should be good. Also if your system exports with non-ASCII spaces, please switch to plain ASCII spaces or digits.
Merridian Finance: Will do now. We appreciate the quick triage.
ACH Bot: //automated// Ticket created: TCK-4458 — ops remediation required for pay_98324.
Lisa (Ops): I'll handle the remediation flow: re-queue after normalization, confirm with bank after re-send, and document in postmortem. Assigning to myself.
Anna (Support): Follow-ups: 1) Raj to PR normalization hotfix 2) Ops to re-send after approval 3) Support to confirm with Merridian when complete.
Raj (Payments Eng): PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/payments-service/pull/1837 — small tests included.
Lisa (Ops): Ops ran a dry-run: normalized routing -> 011000015, re-sent, bank accepted in sandbox. Will schedule live retry pending Merridian consent.
Merridian Finance: Consent provided. Please proceed.
Anna (Support): Marking as in-progress. Will update thread when bank confirms settlement. :white_check_mark:
